title: Empirical Integration of a Formal Network Verifier as an Oracle inside an LLM Generate–Verify–Repair Loop: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired within‑task experiment (study_id netverify_gvr_empirical_integration_2026_v1) to test whether embedding a deterministic network verifier as an oracle inside a bounded LLM Generate–Verify–Repair (GVR) loop increases detection/rejection of unsafe or incorrect LLM‑generated network configurations and improves bounded repair success versus single‑shot generation. Using a synthetic intent→configuration suite (N=270 tasks), gpt-5-mini as generator, and a Dockerized Kathará/Mininet deterministic validator/emulator as ground truth, we observed no verifier rejections: baseline accepted 270/270 (100%); guarded (verify → optional bounded repair) accepted 270/270 (100%); bounded repair was not invoked. Paired difference = 0.00 (paired bootstrap 95% CI [0.00,0.00], exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; bootstrap resamples = 10,000, seed = 1729). The preregistered execution used shared_initial_candidate semantics (independent_condition_generation=false), so a single generated candidate per task was evaluated under both arms; this preregistered design decision is the proximate cause of the degenerate observed contingency and is documented with full execution provenance (preregistration SHA‑256 8ae7fbadf89e5d56671560e43f03c4a92ad5f8c9b8586ac8eb3cc3c8fa00a1c0; master prompt archive SHA‑256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). We release complete preregistration, execution traces, scoring JSONs, and per‑artifact SHA‑256 manifest to enable deterministic reproduction and targeted, minimal-parameter follow‑ups.

sections.introduction: LLM‑assisted intent→configuration pipelines promise to simplify NetOps but raise reliability and safety concerns because LLM generation is stochastic and may produce syntactically plausible yet semantically unsafe device commands. Practical defenses adopt a Generate–Verify–Repair (GVR) architecture: generate candidate configuration(s), deterministically verify correctness/safety with a verifier, and if the verifier rejects, invoke a bounded repair loop that uses verifier diagnostics to guide new generation attempts. We preregistered a confirmatory paired experiment to quantify the marginal effect of inserting a deterministic verifier into an LLM pipeline when tasks are paired within intent and a single generated candidate may or may not differ across arms. Research question: does embedding a formal network verifier as an oracle inside a bounded LLM GVR loop increase the proportion of unsafe or incorrect generated configurations that are detected/rejected, and does bounded repair recover verifier‑accepted outputs more often than single‑shot generation? Contributions: (1) a fully preregistered, artifact‑anchored paired study (study_id netverify_gvr_empirical_integration_2026_v1) with public‑grade provenance (preregistration SHA‑256 8ae7fbad...a1c0; master prompt archive SHA‑256 1872df1e...15ba); (2) a complete execution and scoring bundle (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 43381c4b...) and deterministic hashes for all primary artifacts; (3) an empirical outcome that clarifies how generation semantics (shared_initial_candidate vs independent sampling) controls whether a verifier can change observed accept/reject outcomes, and a reproducible minimal recipe to test the original estimand under independent sampling.
sections.related_work: We position this work among two strands. One strand proposes GVR and related generate‑then‑verify architectures to limit LLM hallucination and enforce formal correctness in compliance‑sensitive domains [Rafael Cadenas, Convergent Correctness; see doi:10.2139/ssrn.6754899]. The second strand provides formal deterministic verification tools and decision procedures for network properties (NetKAT/weighted NetKAT and related quantitative verification) that can serve as deterministic oracles inside GVR pipelines [see Suárez Acevedo et al., doi:10.1145/3808318]. Recent NetOps proposals combine intent life‑cycle ideas, RAG, and verifier anchoring; these motivate our operational study but do not replace the need for preregistered, provenance‑recorded experiments that measure verifier marginal effects under explicit sampling semantics (examples: OpenAlex records W4400072049, W4386722061, W4414359351). Unlike prior work that offers architectural argument or case studies, we executed a preregistered paired test with complete deterministic logging and released every scoring/validator trace so readers can inspect the exact runs that produced the observed contingency.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and frozen plan. The preregistration (study_id netverify_gvr_empirical_integration_2026_v1) was frozen before execution; archived preregistration SHA‑256 8ae7fbadf89e5d56671560e43f03c4a92ad5f8c9b8586ac8eb3cc3c8fa00a1c0. Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (within‑task difference in proportion of verifier rejections/accepts). Design. Paired within‑task (Npairs=270). Task bank. SyntheticNetOpsIntentConfig_v1: 3 vendor syntaxes × 3 topology templates × 30 tasks = 270 tasks; a 20% stratified validation subset (54 tasks) reserved for verifier↔emulator concordance checks. Generator and verifier. Declared generator: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 a40e96e2...); provider recorded as openai_responses. Deterministic verifier: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 executed against a Dockerized Kathará/Mininet emulator used as the definitive emulator ground truth. Execution_contract decisive fields. The frozen execution contract set initial_generation_calls_per_task=1 and independent_condition_generation=false (shared_initial_candidate semantics), maximum_repair_calls_per_task=1, planned_episode_count=540 (270 pairs × 2 conditions), and model_calls_used observed=270. The shared_initial_candidate semantics mean a single generated candidate per task was evaluated in both baseline and guarded arms; this choice is archived and verifiable (execution/execution_manifest.json). Scoring and validation. Each candidate was deterministically validated by the validator which records normalized_configuration, parsed_command_count, touched_field_count, violation codes, and the final validation decision. The scoring JSONs (execution/scoring/*.json) contain the validator_traces for every episode; example files and their SHA‑256s are included in the artifact manifest. Statistical analysis plan. Primary test: paired binary comparison (exact McNemar two‑sided). Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI computed with 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed=1729). Missingness and retry rules. Model/API call failures: up to two retries per failed call (exponential backoff); retries and any infrastructure failures are logged in execution/execution_log.jsonl and the per‑artifact manifest. Repair policy. Guarded arm: upon verifier rejection invoke bounded repair loop with verifier diagnostics; preregistered maximum_repair_calls_per_task=1. All generated responses, repair prompts (if any), provider traces and the full per‑artifact SHA‑256 manifest were archived (see execution/*).

sections.discussion: Why the run produced a provenance‑backed null. Two preregistered decisions jointly produced the degenerate outcome: (1) shared_initial_candidate semantics (execution_contract.independent_condition_generation=false) caused a single generated candidate to be evaluated in both arms; and (2) the chosen generator settings and prompt (declared_model_version gpt-5-mini per execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 a40e96e2...) produced verifier‑acceptable outputs for every synthetic task in the suite. Both facts are archived and verifiable (see execution/execution_manifest.json and execution/raw_results.jsonl). Implications for estimand and power. The preregistered power/MDE calculation assumed independent stochastic generation per arm (independent_condition_generation=true). Because the executed run used shared_initial_candidate, those MDE/power assumptions do not apply to the observed contingency; the observed p=1.0 and CI=[0.00,0.00] are therefore degenerate and must be interpreted as conditional on identical generated candidates. This mismatch is disclosed and archived (preregistration SHA‑256 above). Operational interpretation. The experiment shows a provenance‑grounded boundary condition: when an LLM generator (with the chosen prompt/settings) consistently outputs verifier‑acceptable candidates for the test bank, inserting a deterministic verifier and a bounded repair loop will not change observed accept/reject outcomes under shared‑candidate evaluation. This does not imply verifiers are useless in general; rather, it quantifies a regime (low generator failure rate and shared candidate per pair) where verifier insertion produces no measured improvement. Reproducible minimal follow‑up recipe (artifact‑anchored). To produce an execution that validly tests the original preregistered estimand (marginal verifier effect under independent sampling), change only the following preregistered JSON fields and re‑run the archived harness: (A) set execution_contract.independent_condition_generation=true so each arm receives an independent stochastic generation; (B) set planned_model_calls or maximum_model_calls to 540 (one generation per arm per task) so model_calls_used permits independent sampling; (C) set execution/model_configuration.json temperature to a non‑zero value (or provide a deterministic seed list in the task_manifest) to expose generator sampling variability; (D) optionally increase maximum_repair_calls_per_task > 1 to test bounded repair convergence. All field names and artifact paths referenced here appear in the archived preregistration and execution manifest (execution/execution_manifest.json; model_configuration.json SHA‑256 a40e96e2...). Threats to validity. Internal validity: the shared candidate choice removed between‑arm stochasticity and thus altered the estimand the power calculation targeted. Construct validity: synthetic tasks capture common operational patterns (shutdown→change→restore, make‑before‑break) but do not substitute for multi‑vendor production heterogeneity. External validity: single model (gpt-5-mini) and single verifier rule set were used. Conclusion validity: zero discordant pairs preclude informative hypothesis rejection and make the original power calculation inapplicable; this is recorded in analysis artifacts and the deterministic reconciliation file.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered, artifact‑anchored paired study integrating a deterministic network verifier into an LLM GVR pipeline and released the complete provenance bundle. Under the executed shared_initial_candidate semantics and the chosen generator/settings the single generated candidate per task was verifier‑acceptable for all N=270 tasks so the verifier/repair path was not invoked; the observed paired difference is 0.00 (95% bootstrap CI [0.00,0.00]; McNemar p=1.0). This provenance‑backed null identifies a concrete evaluation regime in which a deterministic verifier, as deployed here, does not change measured accept/reject outcomes. The primary scientific lesson is methodological: generation semantics (shared candidate vs independent sampling) critically determine whether a verifier insertion is testable under the preregistered estimand. We publish the exact artifacts and a minimal reproducible recipe (change execution_contract.independent_condition_generation to true; increase model calls; vary temperature/seeds; optionally increase repair budget) so the community can deterministically explore the regime where verifier/repair utility will be observed. All execution, scoring, and analysis artifacts are archived and hashed for deterministic reproduction (see execution/execution_manifest.json and analysis/*).

limitations: Synthetic task suite and limited operational realism: results may not generalize to complex, noisy, adversarial, or production NetOps environments; emulator behavior can differ from heterogeneous production devices.
Single‑model evaluation: only a single generator (gpt-5-mini) was used; no claim of multi‑model generality should be inferred.

Generation semantics constraint: the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (independent_condition_generation=false) produced one generated candidate per task and thereby eliminated between‑arm stochastic sampling variance; the preregistered MDE calculations assumed independent sampling and are therefore inapplicable to the observed contingency.

Bounded repair budget: the repair loop allowed at most one repair call per rejected candidate (maximum_repair_calls_per_task=1); multi‑attempt repair strategies were not evaluated and could change outcomes.

Verifier rule‑set sensitivity: a single deterministic verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) and rule set were used; different verifier conservatism or policy choices will change false‑accept/reject tradeoffs.
Emulator vs production gap: emulator‑validated safety does not guarantee identical behavior on production devices or multi‑vendor deployments.
